title: Achieve near-complete plaque psoriasis clearance through IL-17 blockade

concept.text: Produce near-complete skin clearance in a large proportion of people with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis through targeted biologic treatment. This is disease control during treatment, rather than permanent immune tolerance. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by randomized trials meeting PASI75 and clear/almost-clear investigator endpoints, with at least half of treated patients achieving PASI90 at week 12. Test set by: FDA sets approval; pivotal investigators prespecified the psoriasis endpoints. The majority-PASI90 boundary is an editorial criterion, not an FDA licensing minimum. Reported achieved: FDA approved secukinumab (Cosentyx) on 21 January 2015; the 300 mg groups achieved PASI90 in 59% and 54% in two pivotal trials. Overlaps: DER-03, IMM-04. Sources given: [FDA Cosentyx original approval package](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125504Orig1s000Approv.pdf) ; [Cosentyx prescribing information and PASI outcomes](https://www.dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=77c4b13e-7df3-42d4-81db-3d0cddb7f67a&type=display).

page.title: First IL-17 inhibitor licensed for plaque psoriasis
page.definition: A biologic medicine is licensed to treat adults with plaque psoriasis by blocking an interleukin-17 (IL-17) inflammatory signal at the cytokine or its receptor. The first was secukinumab, an antibody that neutralises IL-17A. Its trials measured skin response with the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI), which combines affected area, redness, thickness and scaling. PASI 75 and PASI 90 mean reductions of at least 75% and 90% from baseline.

goal.need: Psoriasis in all its forms affected an estimated 100 million people worldwide in 2016. Among 2,077 adults with plaque psoriasis in placebo-controlled trials, 45% had already had an inadequate response to a nonbiologic treatment. Blocking IL-17A offers another option for adults with moderate-to-severe plaques, including some whose disease persisted despite a TNF inhibitor. Patients can experience less itching, pain and scaling during treatment. Skin improvement can diminish after dosing stops.

figures.caption: Baseline characteristics in four placebo-controlled secukinumab trials
figures.note: These figures describe trial participants with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, rather than population prevalence.

statements.body: Medical Board of the National Psoriasis Foundation
statements.quote: The target response at 3 months postinitiation was BSA 1% or less.
statements.context: BSA means body surface area. The consensus involved 25 psoriasis experts and was published online on 28 November 2016.

statements.body: European Medicines Agency, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use
statements.quote: recommends the granting of the marketing authorisation.
statements.context: The committee's 20 November opinion concerned secukinumab for adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who were candidates for systemic therapy.

completion.title: A medicines authority grants the first marketing authorisation for an IL-17 inhibitor for plaque psoriasis.
completion.criterion: A competent medicines authority grants marketing authorisation for at least one medicine that directly inhibits an IL-17 cytokine or its receptor. The approved indication must cover treatment of plaque psoriasis in adults, subject to the treatment restrictions in that jurisdiction. The earliest qualifying authorisation in any one jurisdiction meets the test.
completion.set_by: The medicines authority in the licensing jurisdiction. Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare granted the first authorisation, recorded in the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency's FY 2014 list of approved new drugs, item 56.
completion.threshold_quote: indicated for the treatment of plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis
completion.basis: The decisive event is a licence covering the skin indication. Japan licensed secukinumab on 26 December 2014 for plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis after an inadequate response to conventional therapy. FDA approval followed on 21 January 2015. The week-12 PASI and investigator assessments belong to the pivotal trial milestone.

milestones.title: An IL-17 antibody has laboratory activity and toxicology supporting exposure in humans.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical studies establish the intended biological activity of an IL-17 antibody and characterise its toxicity in a pharmacologically relevant species, as ICH S6 asks before human exposure: an assay in human cells shows neutralisation of IL-17 signalling with a stated potency, and a repeat-dose toxicity study in a relevant species assigns a no-observed-adverse-effect level. A regulator's pharmacology and toxicology review or a peer-reviewed report documents both. One of the two is partial.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, ICH S6 sections 1.2 and 3.1–3.3, retained in S6(R1). The guidance covers nonclinical work before and throughout clinical development.
milestones.threshold_quote: The objectives of the preclinical safety studies are to define pharmacological and toxicological effects

milestones.title: An IL-17A antibody improves PASI and IGA versus placebo at four weeks in adults with plaque psoriasis.
milestones.criterion: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled proof-of-concept study in adults with chronic plaque psoriasis shows that an antibody against IL-17A improves both the PASI score and the Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) more than placebo four weeks after dosing (P < 0.05 for each), and reports the number of participants per group.
milestones.set_by: Novartis and participating investigators, psoriasis proof-of-concept protocol published by Hueber and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: In the psoriasis study, the co-primary endpoints were PASI and IGA at week 4.

milestones.title: An IL-17A antibody increases week-12 PASI75 responses over placebo in a dose-finding trial.
milestones.criterion: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose-finding trial in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis shows that at least one regimen of an IL-17A antibody gives a higher proportion of patients with PASI 75, at least 75% improvement from baseline, than placebo after 12 weeks (P < 0.05), and reports the response for each regimen.
milestones.set_by: Novartis and participating investigators, phase II dose-ranging protocol published by Papp and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary efficacy outcome was at least 75% improvement from baseline in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index score (PASI 75)

milestones.title: An IL-17 inhibitor meets week-12 PASI75 and clear/almost-clear endpoints in two pivotal trials.
milestones.criterion: Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal trials in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis each show an IL-17 inhibitor superior to placebo at week 12 on both co-primary endpoints: PASI 75, and an IGA modified 2011 score of 0 or 1, meaning clear or almost clear skin with at least a two-grade improvement. The analysis controls the family-wise type I error at 0.05 across doses and endpoints. One trial, or one of the two endpoints, is partial.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Statistical Review and Evaluation for BLA 125504/0, assessing the prespecified ERASURE and FIXTURE efficacy tests.
milestones.threshold_quote: PASI 75 response at Week 12 and IGA 0 or 1 at Week 12

milestones.title: A regulatory review body recommends approval of an IL-17 inhibitor for adult plaque psoriasis.
milestones.criterion: Before the licensing decision, a medicines agency's scientific review body or advisory committee issues a formal favourable conclusion on the application. Its report or recorded vote must support approval of the IL-17 inhibitor for an indication covering plaque psoriasis in adults after consideration of benefit and risk.
milestones.set_by: Japan's Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency and Second Committee on New Drugs, the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, and the FDA's advisory committee, in their respective pre-authorisation reviews.
milestones.threshold_quote:
the product may
be approved for “Indications” and “Dosage and administration” as shown below

milestones.title: An IL-17 inhibitor suppresses an IL-17-induced response in a cell assay.
milestones.criterion: A functional assay in cultured cells shows that the candidate reduces a response induced by IL-17. The assay measures a downstream cellular response, such as cytokine release, and compares that response with and without the inhibitor.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, ICH S6(R1), section 3.2, on in vitro biological activity. The secukinumab pharmacology review documents a quantitative application.
milestones.threshold_quote: Biological activity may be evaluated using in vitro assays

milestones.title: Nonclinical safety data support a starting dose of the IL-17 inhibitor for human studies.
milestones.criterion: Toxicology studies in a pharmacologically relevant species characterise potential adverse effects at the exposures tested and support the proposed initial human dose and dose escalation. Species relevance depends on the candidate's biological activity in that species.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, ICH S6(R1), sections 1.2 and 3.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: to identify an initial safe dose and subsequent dose escalation schemes in humans

not_found: No requirement that at least half of treated patients achieve PASI90 at week 12 was found in FDA's approval letter, original label or statistical review.

results.finding: Secukinumab: repeat-dose toxicity in cynomolgus monkeys (4/sex/group) established a NOAEL of 50 mg/kg/week.
results.detail: Human synoviocytes showed inhibition of IL-17A/TNFα-induced IL-6 release with IC50 0.14 ±0.02 nM. Cynomolgus monkeys were pharmacologically relevant; the pivotal study involved 26 weeks of weekly intravenous dosing and 13 weeks of recovery.
results.quote:
Secukinumab at picomolar concentrations potently inhibited the IL-6 release from 
human synoviocytes when induced by IL-17A (30 pM)/TNFα costimulation with an IC50
value of 0.14 ±0.02 nM.

results.finding: Secukinumab repeat-dose toxicity in monkeys (sample size unstated) yielded an apparent NOAEL of 50 mg/kg/week.
results.detail: The review identifies cynomolgus monkeys as pharmacologically relevant and describes 26-week repeat-dose toxicity. It does not report a human-cell neutralisation assay with stated potency.
results.quote:
Due to clinical chemistry effects and 
immunotoxicity (decreases in total lymphocytes, B cells and T cells) observed at the 
high dose, the NOAEL appears to be 50 mg/kg/week.

results.finding: Secukinumab inhibited IL-6 release in IL-17A/TNFα-stimulated human synoviocytes with an IC50 of 0.14 nM (sample size unreported).
results.quote:
Secukinumab at picomolar concentrations potently inhibited the IL-6 release from 
human synoviocytes when induced by IL-17A (30 pM)/TNFα costimulation with an IC50
value of 0.14 ±0.02 nM.

results.finding: Secukinumab had an apparent NOAEL of 50 mg/kg/week in the pivotal repeat-dose study in cynomolgus monkeys (n=8 per main-study group).
results.detail: The human dose comparison uses a dose already administered. The excerpt gives no first-in-human dose-selection or escalation rationale.
results.quote:
Based on these 
data, the NOAEL appears to be 50 mg/kg/week.

results.finding: FDA pharmacology/toxicology reviewers found secukinumab approvable for severe plaque psoriasis in BLA 125504 (no participant sample for this recommendation).
results.quote:
COSENTYX is approvable for the treatment of severe plaque psoriasis from a 
pharmacology/toxicology perspective.

results.finding: Secukinumab beat placebo on both week-12 co-primary endpoints in two pivotal trials (N=2,044 total, p<0.0001 for each comparison).
results.detail: The FDA reviewer's analysis included all randomized participants in the efficacy population and counted missing week-12 outcomes as nonresponses.
results.quote:
Both secukinumab 300 mg and 150 mg were superior to placebo at Week 12 (p<0.0001) 
for the co-primary endpoints of PASI 75 response and IGA of 0 or 1, as well as the key 
secondary endpoint of PASI 90 response at Week 12 in both Trials 2302 and 2303.

results.finding: Secukinumab caused no observed embryofetal toxicity in cynomolgus monkeys at maternal doses up to 150 mg/kg. Sample size unreported.
results.detail: The label expresses the monkey dose margin relative to the maximum recommended human dose on a mg/kg basis. It gives no first-in-human dose rationale.
results.quote:
Developmental toxicity studies 
conducted with monkeys found no evidence of harm to the fetus due to secukinumab.

results.finding: Secukinumab 300 mg achieved week-12 PASI 75 in 82% of recipients in Trial 1 (n=245).
results.detail: Trial 1 arm sizes were 245, 245, and 248 for 300 mg, 150 mg, and placebo. Trial 2 arm sizes were 327, 327, and 326, with a separate active-control arm.

results.finding: FDA initially approved secukinumab for adult plaque psoriasis in 2015.
Secukinumab had an apparent no-observed-adverse-effect level of 50 mg/kg/week in cynomolgus monkeys, with 8 animals per group.
results.detail: The review reports decreased natural killer cell activity at the middle and high doses and immunotoxicity in one high-dose female.
results.quote:
Based on these data, the NOAEL 
appears to be 50 mg/kg/week with an AUC0-168 hr of 316000 μg ●hr/mL.

results.finding: Phase 2 secukinumab data supported testing 150 mg in Phase 3. The review gives no sample size for the week-12 response signal.
results.quote:
The Phase 2 efficacy data overall supported the selection of the 150 mg 
dose to be tested in Phase 3 and suggested that early induction doses could achieve a 
higher clinical response rate at Week 12.

results.finding: Secukinumab beat placebo on both week-12 co-primary endpoints in two pivotal trials (n=738 and n=1,306), with P < 0.0001.
results.quote:
Both secukinumab 300 mg and 150 mg were superior to placebo (p<0.0001) for the co-
primary endpoints of PASI 75 response and IGA of 0 or 1 in each of the pivotal trials.

results.finding: The CHMP recommended secukinumab for adult plaque psoriasis on 20 November 2014. The report gives no committee vote count.
results.quote:
On 20 November 2014, the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) 
adopted a positive opinion, recommending the granting of a marketing authorization for 
the medicinal product Cosentyx

results.finding: Secukinumab had a NOAEL of 50 mg/kg/week in cynomolgus monkeys, with 8 animals per group in the pivotal repeat-dose study.
results.detail: The review compares an administered clinical dose with one-tenth of the monkey NOAEL. It does not identify that dose as the proposed starting dose.
results.quote: Based on these data, the NOAEL appears to be 50 mg/kg/week.

results.finding: Secukinumab outperformed placebo on both week-12 co-primary endpoints in 2 pivotal trials enrolling 738 and 1,306 adults.
results.detail: Trial 2303's total includes the etanercept arm. The reported p<0.0001 for that comparator does not establish multiplicity control for the placebo comparisons.
results.quote:
Secukinumab, at doses of 300 mg and 150 mg, was superior to placebo in the treatment of 
moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in two Phase 3 trials (2302 and 2303), with Trial 2303 
including an etanercept comparator arm.

results.finding: All 7 FDA advisory committee voters supported secukinumab approval for eligible adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
The FDA approved one IL-17A inhibitor, secukinumab, for eligible adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis on January 21, 2015.
results.quote: We have approved your BLA for COSENTYX™ (secukinumab) effective this date.

results.finding: Cynomolgus monkey toxicology for izokibep (animal n unreported) supported a 2 mg first-in-human starting dose.
results.detail: The starting-dose rationale comes from the 28-day GLP IV study. The paper reports the clinical escalation schedule without giving a nonclinical safety margin for the higher doses.
results.quote: A starting dose of 2 mg was supported by the NOAEL from the 28-day non-human primate good laboratory practice toxicity study (387-fold safety margin).

results.finding: Bimekizumab suppressed IL-17F plus TNF-induced IL-6 release in human dermal fibroblasts (3 experiments, duplicate wells per condition), with an IC90 of 137.8 ng/mL.
results.detail: IL-17F alone elicited too little IL-6 for the assay. Costimulation with TNF produced a stronger response, and IL-6 was measured in the culture supernatant after 18–20 h.
results.quote:
Of note, only 496.g3 demonstrated inhibition of IL-17F (IC
90
137.8 ng/mL), as neither ixekizumab nor secukinumab bound IL-17F

results.finding: On 20 November 2014, CHMP recommended approval of secukinumab for adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis eligible for systemic therapy. No vote count was reported.
results.quote:
The CHMP, on the basis of quality, safety and efficacy data submitted, considers there to be a 
favourable benefit-to-risk balance for Cosentyx and therefore recommends the granting of the 
marketing authorisation.
